classifications.reason: The exception for devices moved by human power describes this class's human-powered wheeled vehicles.
The admitting clause reaches motor vehicles designed to transport passengers, and no exception describes this class.
This class describes a person, whereas the admitting clause reaches transportation devices rather than the people transported.
The admitting clause reaches the transportation vehicles described by this contract, and neither commercial mass nor commercial licensing is an exception.
The definition expressly names electric bicycles among its exceptions.
The definition expressly names an electric scooter among its exceptions.
The admitting clause reaches the vehicles described by this contract without requiring emergency-response conduct, and no exception describes the class.
A fire-fighting vehicle fits the admitting clause for transportation devices, and no exception describes this class.

The admitting clause and the quoted description of a motor-driven scooter, cycle or similar vehicle reach jurisdiction-classed mopeds, whose posted definition distinguishes them from electric bicycles and electric scooters.
The admitting clause reaches this class's self-propelled transportation vehicles, and no exception describes its nonrail contract with separately classed powered two-wheelers excluded.
Motor vehicles ridden astride on two or three wheels fit the admitting clause, and no exception names or describes the motorcycle class.
The admitting clause reaches vehicles in official or contracted road service, and no exception concerns their service role.
The contract describes a person rather than a transportation device, including when that person uses a wheelchair or another pedestrian device.
The contract describes a pedestrian person rather than a device, and using a cane, guide animal or human guide does not bring that person within the admitting words.
The exception for devices used exclusively upon stationary rails describes the trains, trams, streetcars and other on-track equipment in this contract.
A bus designated to carry school children fits the admitting clause for passenger-transport devices, and no exception describes this class.
A passenger vehicle for hire fits the admitting clause, and its hire status or markings do not match any exception.
Both the passenger buses and lengthened passenger vehicles described by this contract fit the admitting clause, with no applicable class exception.
The admitting clause expressly reaches devices by which persons or property may be transported or drawn, encompassing the drawn vehicles and combinations described by this contract.
A bus in public transit service fits the admitting clause for passenger-transport devices, and no exception concerns transit service.
A motor vehicle built to carry goods fits the admitting clause for property-transport devices, and no exception describes this class.
